method: Every live fact was read as one line (claim, displays, kind, hard, relevance, source page); candidate duplicates were grouped by overlapping quote spans and claim-token similarity. Decisions are in reg-decisions.json; patches in reg-patches/ (built by reg_build.py, which checks every display against normalize_text of the quotes and the 8-word rule); applied through saa.py by reg_apply.py (log: reg-apply.log.jsonl). Demand statuses merged by reg_demand.py.
rules_applied: Duplicates: superseded when two facts quote the same sentence of the same page or state the same rule from two pages of the same kind (kept the more direct or longer span and the better displays). FAQ facts that repeat a guide sentence were kept for the FAQ quick-fire, except lambda-snapstart-java-no-charge (pricing page), merged into the FAQ fact that adds the 14-day cache.

Namespace: two RDS Proxy facts quoted from the RDS user guide were superseded by the existing rds-proxy facts (chapter 26). Fargate-versus-Lambda comparison facts from the decision guide stay in lambda (note on lambda-vs-fargate-cpu-memory-ceilings).
Displays without a number: a verbatim phrase of at most 8 words from one quote (RULINGS 2026-10-11); 49 long displays were shortened, 1 dropped, 8 added.
Qualifiers: scope filled on 49 FAQ facts that had none.

Relevance: lambda-sqs-timeout-not-above-visibility and lambda-scaling-rate-not-adjustable raised to core after they absorbed core duplicates; lambda-scaling-rate-not-adjustable took the 2023 scaling change item and volatility frequently-changing.

Claims cut to their evidence: lambda-faq-vpc-no-internet-by-default (the FAQ's 'use internet gateways' sentence removed from claim and evidence), lambda-provisioned-concurrency-charges (display now verbatim 'incurs charges to your AWS account').
